raw_text:
Here is a structured 12-week, low-impact strength program tailored for a 36-year-old male recreational lifter with a prior right medial meniscus tear. This plan prioritizes knee-friendly loading, gradual tissue adaptation, and a smooth progression back toward skiing. It avoids jumping and deep knee flexion under load, and emphasizes control, tempo, and joint health. Acknowledge that he should keep communicating with his surgeon/physio if any flare-ups occur.

Overview
- Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Foundation and pain-free loading
- Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Progressive overload with controlled stimuli
- Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Strength peak and sport-specific readiness
- Weekly structure: 3 strength days (Mon/Wed/Fri or Tue/Thu/Sat) + optional mobility/restorative day
- Primary emphasis: squats and hinge patterns performed with cue-based, shallow knee flexion under load, no plyometrics, and no deep knee flexion beyond 45–60 degrees in loaded sets.
- Reps/sets: Reps vary by phase; progression via load and tempo rather than reps alone.
- Recovery: 1-2 days between heavy sessions; include soft-tissue work, mobility, and anterior knee control.

Important notes before starting
- Pain guidance: If pain (not soreness) increases in or around the knee, stop that exercise and reassess technique or substitute.
- Range and depth: No deep knee flexion under load. For squats, use a heel-elevated box squat or a shallow goblet squat to a comfortable depth (~ 30–45 degrees knee flexion) as initial loading.
- Knee tracking: Focus on knee tracking over the middle of the foot; avoid valgus collapse.
- Warm-up: 8–12 minutes of light cardio (bike, elliptical) plus dynamic warm-up for hips, ankles, and knees; finish with activation drills.

Weekly progression framework
- Weeks 1–4: Build technique, normalize movement patterns, establish baseline strength with conservative loads.
- Weeks 5–8: Increase load and introduce tempo work to increase time under tension.
- Weeks 9–12: Peak strength with higher loads, maintain controlled ROM, and introduce sport-specific elements (as tolerable) with no jumping or deep flexion.

Phase 1: Foundation and pain-free loading (Weeks 1–4)
Goals: establish solid technique, reintroduce strength with low knee flexion, build confidence, and begin tissue adaptation.

Weeks 1–2
Day A (Lower Body Focus)
- Goblet Squat: 3 sets x 8–10 reps; tempo 3–0-1-0; focus on upright torso, shallow depth (~30–45° knee flexion), brace core.
- Incline Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift: 3x10 (to keep knee out of deep flexion while training hamstrings)
- Supported Split Squat (rear foot elevated if tolerated): 3x8 per leg; depth shallow
- Hip Thrust or Glute Bridge: 3x12
- Seated Leg Curl (machine): 3x12 (control)
- Calf Raise: 3x15

Day B (Upper Body + Core)
- Flat Dumbbell Press: 3x8–10
- Barbell Row or One-Arm Dumbbell Row: 3x8–10
- Overhead Press (neutral grip if possible): 3x8
- Pallof press (anti-rotation): 3x10 per side
- Farmer’s Carry: 3 x 30–45s
- Plank: 3 x 30–45s

Weeks 3–4
Day A
- Goblet Squat: 4x8–10; tempo 2–0-1-0 (slightly deeper if tolerated)
- Romanian Deadlift (DB or bar): 3x8–10
- Split Squat (heel-right dominant if tolerates): 3x8 per leg
- Hip Thrust: 3x12
- Lying Leg Curl: 3x12
- Calf Raise: 3x15

Day B
- Incline Press or Flat DB Press: 3x8–10
- Dumbbell Row: 3x8–10
- Seated Dumbbell Shoulder Press: 3x8–10
- Anti-Rotation: Pallof 3x12 per side
- Farmer’s Carry: 3x40–50s
- Side Plank: 3x20–30s per side

Phase 2: Progressive overload with tempo work (Weeks 5–8)
Goals: increase load while maintaining controlled knee depth and avoiding high impact.

Weeks 5–6
Day A
- Box Squat (to a comfortable height, or shallow goblet squat if box depth not suitable): 4x6–8; tempo 2–0-1-0
- Romanian Deadlift (DB or Bar): 3x6–8
- Split Squat or Bulgarian Split Squat (shallow depth): 3x6–8 per leg
- Hip Thrust: 4x8
- Leg Curl: 3x10–12
- Calf Raise: 3x12–15

Day B
- Bench Press or DB Floor Press (to minimize shoulder strain): 3x6–8
- Barbell/DB Row: 3x6–8
- Push-ups (inclined if needed): 3x8–10
- Pallof press: 3x12 per side
- Farmer’s Carry: 3x45–60s
- Anti-extension holds (dead bug progression or ab wheel if tolerable): 3x8–10 reps

Weeks 7–8
Day A
- Front Squat or Box Squat: 4x5–7; tempo 2–0-1-0
- Romanian Deadlift or Sumo RDL: 3x6–8
- Split Squat (moderate depth): 3x6 per leg
- Hip Thrust: 4x8
- Leg Curl: 3x10
- Calf Raise: 3x12–15

Day B
- Incline DB Press: 3x6–8
- Barbell/DB Row: 3x6–8
- Shoulder Press: 3x6–8
- Pallof press or Suitcase carry: 3x12 per side
- Farmer’s Carry: 3x50–70s
- Plank variation (front planks or side planks): 3x30–45s

Phase 3: Strength peak and sport-readiness (Weeks 9–12)
Goals: lift heavier with refined technique; introduce sport-specific patterns without jumping or deep knee flexion.

Weeks 9–10
Day A
- Box Squat or Front Squat (limit depth): 4x4–6; tempo 1–0-1-0
- RDL (DB/Bar): 4x6
- Split Squat or Reverse Lunge (shallow): 3x6 per leg
- Hip Thrust: 4x8
- Leg Curl: 3x8–10
- Calf Raise: 3x12

Day B
- Flat/Incline Press: 4x5–6
- Row (Pendlay or Barbell Row): 4x5–6
- Accessory Push (DB Floor Press or Push-up progressions): 3x6–8
- Pallof press or Single-arm carry: 3x12 per side
- Farmer’s Carry: 3x60–75s
- Core stability: 3x45s dead bug or hollow hold

Weeks 11–12
Day A
- Box Squat or Front Squat: 4x4–6; aim to maintain depth control
- RDL: 4x6
- Split Squat or Bulgarian Split Squat: 3x6 per leg
- Hip Thrust: 4x8
- Hamstring Curl: 3x8–10
- Calf Raise: 3x12–15

Day B
- Pressing Complex: e.g., DB floor press 3x6, followed by 3x6 row
- Barbell Row: 4x6
- Shoulder Strengther: 3x6–8 (lateral raises limited by shoulder tolerance)
- Anti- rotation: Pallof 3x12
- Farmer’s Carry: 3x60–75s
- Core: 3x45s side planks

Exercise selection notes
- Squat patterns: Use goblet, front, or box squats with shallow depth to protect knee cartilage and ligaments. If depth is allowed by surgeon/physio, you may progress depth modestly but never past 45–60 degrees knee flexion under load.
- Hinge patterns: RDLs and hip thrusts develop posterior chain without loading the knee deeply.
- Lunges/step variations: Keep depth shallow; consider reverse lunges with short stance.
- Calf work: Important for impact absorption in skiing; include calf raises regularly.
- Core and anti-rotational work: Pallof presses, planks, dead bugs to maintain trunk stability.

Volume and progression strategy
- Reps: Gradually increase load while keeping reps within prescribed ranges per phase.
- Intensity: Use RPE 6–8 for most sets in phases 1–2; Phase 3 can push to RPE 8–9 for near-max effort on main lifts, but avoid knee pain.
- Tempo: Emphasize controlled tempo (2–0–1–0 to 3–0–1–0) to increase time under tension and protect the knee.
- Rest: 60–120 seconds between main sets; 90–180 seconds on heavier sets.

Weekly plan structure (example)
- Day 1: Lower Body A (Weeks 1–4) or Day A adjusted per phase
- Day 2: Upper Body A (Weeks 1–12)
- Day 3: Lower Body B (Weeks 1–4 adjust; Weeks 5–12)
- Optional mobility/restorative day: 20–40 minutes light cardio and mobility work

Sample week (Week 5, as a concrete example)
- Day 1: Lower Body A
  - Box Squat: 4x6–8; tempo 2–0-1-0
  - RDL: 3x6–8
  - Split Squat: 3x6 per leg
  - Hip Thrust: 4x8
  - Leg Curl: 3x10
  - Calf Raise: 3x12
- Day 2: Upper Body A
  - Flat DB Press: 3x6–8
  - DB Row: 3x6–8
  - Overhead Press: 3x6–8
  - Pallof press: 3x12 per side
  - Farmer’s Carry: 3x60s
  - Plank: 3x45s
- Day 3: Lower Body B
  - Front Squat: 4x5–7; tempo 2–0-1-0
  - Romanian Deadlift: 3x6–8
  - Split Squat: 3x6 per leg
  - Hip Thrust: 4x8
  - Leg Curl: 3x10
  - Calf Raise: 3x12

Nutrition and recovery guidance
- Protein: 1.6–2.2 g/kg body weight daily to support tissue repair and gains. Spread across 3–4 meals with some protein post-workout.
- Carbohydrates: Moderate intake to fuel workouts; adjust based on energy and recovery. Include timing around workouts (half to full-carb meal post-workout if training intensity is high).
- Fats: Ensure essential fats; keep total fat sufficient for hormones and joint health.
- Hydration: 2–3 liters per day, more on training days.
- Supplements: Creatine monohydrate 3–5 g daily can help strength and tissue adaptation; consider omega-3s for joint health; consult clinician regarding NSAID use.
- Sleep: Aim for 7–9 hours per night to support recovery.
- Mobility and recovery:
  - 10–15 minutes post-workout of mobility work for hips, ankles, and knees.
  - Optional weekly soft-tissue work (foam rolling) for quads, glutes, hamstrings.
  - Include 1–2 days of light aerobic work (e.g., cycling, brisk walking) to support recovery.

Knee-specific considerations
- Range of motion: Avoid deep knee flexion under load; use supportive depth and progress gradually.
- Pain monitoring: If any swelling or sharp pain arises, pause the agonist pattern and consult with the client’s medical team.
- Ski-specific preparation: In later weeks, include ski-precision drills at the gym such as single-leg stance on unstable surface with light resistance, focus on knee tracking and control; avoid explosive or high-impact actions.

Return-to-ski readiness criteria (end of Week 12)
- Demonstrated confidence in squats, deadlifts, and split squats with loaded knee depth within safe limits.
- Able to perform controlled leg loading and single-leg work without knee pain or swelling.
- Progress with sport-specific motion: trunk rotation, hip stability, and midline control in skiing posture.
- Comfortable with gradually reintroducing low-impact plyometrics on a progressive timeline (subject to surgeon/physio clearance).

If you want, I can tailor the exact weekly layout to fit the client’s schedule (e.g., M/W/F vs Tue/Thu/Sat), available equipment (barbell vs dumbbells, machines), and any other injuries or limitations.
